YouTube title seed: How Does a Key Actually Open a Lock?
YouTube description seed: Your key has a pattern of cuts. Guess what each one is pushing on inside the lock. #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
The central fact: The key's cuts lift tiny split pins until every split lines up, and only then can the lock turn.
The later surprise: A wrong key leaves pins crossing the line, so even a key that looks almost right stays stuck.
The very first frame shows a brass key sliding into a front-door lock with a light metallic scrape, viewed from the side. It is already moving in the first frame, and nothing in the first second gives the answer away.
What changes inside each 6s clip:
Scene 1 (contradiction, 0-6s): Opening: the key already sliding in. About 2s in, a different key tries the same lock and will not turn; about 4s in, the first key slides back in.
Scene 2 (clue, 6-12s): Mechanism starts about 5s in. A real clear acrylic practice lock (real parts or physical props only, no animation or cutaway graphics) held up to window light with the pins visible; about 2-3s later, framing tightens on the uneven row of pins; then the key's cuts in profile, side by side with the pins.
Scene 3 (mechanism, 12-18s): The key slides into the clear practice lock; about 2s in, each pin pair rises to a different height; about 4s in, the splits line up and the plug turns.
Scene 4 (second_reveal, 18-24s): A nearly identical wrong key in the clear practice lock; about 2s in, the pins stop at uneven heights with some still crossing the line; about 4s in, the plug stays stuck when a hand tries to turn it.
Scene 5 (payoff, 24-30s): The right key goes back into the clear practice lock; about 2s in, the splits line up and the plug turns; about 4s in, cut to the exact opening: the same brass key starting to slide into the same front-door lock from the same side view, matching scene 1's first frame, so it loops.
Fact boundaries: Describe pin tumbler locks only; other lock types work differently. No lock-picking or bypass instructions. Use a clear practice lock as a physical prop; do not show a real door being opened without its key.

facts.statement: In a pin tumbler lock, pairs of small spring-loaded pins sit across the line between the turning plug and the fixed housing, and that blocks the plug from turning.
The cuts on the right key lift each pin pair just enough that the split between the two pins lines up with that line, so the plug can turn and move the bolt.
A wrong key lifts the pins to the wrong heights, so some pins still cross the line and the plug stays stuck.
